title: Admin request orchestration with interactive triage wizard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Many enterprise customers open ad-hoc admin/access requests that are ambiguous, lack context, or require manual research by Support/SE. This increases time-to-resolution, leads to avoidable escalations to Eng, and creates variability in SLA attainment.

Goal:
Build an interactive triage wizard and orchestration layer in the admin intake flow that: (1) collects structured context for RBAC/SSO/SCIM/org-policy requests, (2) computes a risk-and-effort score to determine SLA and routing, (3) suggests standard remediation steps or automated actions when safe, and (4) auto-assigns and surfaces required artifacts to the assignee/support engineer.

Proposed solution (high level):
- A lightweight multi-step wizard embedded in the Admin Request form that dynamically shows questions based on request type (RBAC change, SSO integration, SCIM sync, org policy exception).
- A scoring engine (rules + ML heuristics) that produces three outputs: risk_score (low/medium/high), estimated_engineering_effort (S/M/L), and recommended SLA bucket (48h/7d/30d).
- Rulebook-based auto-actions for low-risk cases: e.g., auto-generate SCIM sample mapping, return template SAML metadata, or trigger a policy rollback when safe.
- Auto-assignment rules: route to Support Tier 2 for S/M effort low-risk; route to Platform Security/Onboarding for high-risk or org-wide changes; route to Eng when estimated_engineering_effort == L. Include escalation timers matching SLA.
- UX: show a summary card with required artifacts (logs, sample manifests, customer org ID) and one-click links to create a follow-up GH issue or start a dedicated private workspace when debugging is needed.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Wizard is feature-flagged and available to 25% of enterprise customers in staging.
2) For 80% of intake submissions, the wizard returns a risk_score and recommended SLA without requiring freeform follow-up.
3) Auto-assigned queue accuracy >= 90% in pilot cohort (measured by reassign rate within 72h).
4) Support time-to-first-response decreases by 25% for pilot customers vs baseline.
5) Low-risk auto-actions successfully resolve >= 60% of eligible requests without human intervention.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implement minimal wizard skeleton + backend scoring service and rules engine. Internal demo with Support and SE teams.
- Week 2: Pilot enabling for 10 strategic enterprise customers via feature flag; collect labeling for scoring engine.
- Week 4: Iterate rules/heuristics, add recommended remediation templates, expand to 25% pilot.
- Week 8: Broader rollout controlled by a configurable quota and admin opt-in; instrument metrics and rollback hooks.

Telemetry & success metrics:
- Intake completion rate, time-to-complete form, % of submissions with structured context filled.
- Risk score distribution and correlation with reassigns/escalations.
- Time-to-first-response and time-to-resolution per SLA bucket.
- Auto-action success rate and false positive rate.

Stakeholders:

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should auto-actions be? We need conservative defaults to avoid making destructive changes.
- Where does the scoring engine live (customer-facing service vs internal routing service)? Keep it internal to avoid exposing model details.
- Labeling data: start with rule-based seed then augment with anonymized historical intake data.
